video.title: What is data science?: Questions, data and answers
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Charts draw themselves; code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello - primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Narrator - the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: Every Monday, half my class arrives late. The head teacher asked me why. I had a guess: maybe pupils are tired after the weekend. But a guess is not an answer. So I asked the data.
Today: what data science is, and how a teacher can use it.
Data science means using data to answer a question. Data engineers collect and store the data. Data scientists ask it questions, find patterns, and explain what they mean.

scenes.on_screen_text: The loop: ask, collect, explore, explain
scenes.narration: Data science is a loop with four steps. Ask a clear question. Collect the data you need. Explore it with numbers and charts. Then explain what you found, and ask the next question.

I took my register and counted late arrivals for four weeks, day by day. Monday had twelve, the other days only about three. The pattern was clear, and it was not tiredness, because Friday was fine too.
So I asked the next question: how do the late pupils travel? Most came on the same bus. On Mondays, it leaves the market late. The data led us to the real cause.
A good data question is clear, you can measure it, and it is about something you can act on. Are pupils happy is hard to measure. How many pupils arrive late, on which days, is easy.

scenes.on_screen_text: Which is a good data question?
scenes.narration: Quick check! Which is the better data question for a class: do pupils like reading, or how many books did each pupil borrow this term?

scenes.on_screen_text: Books borrowed: you can count it
scenes.narration: Books borrowed this term. You can count it from the library cards, and compare classes. Liking reading matters too, but you would need a careful survey to measure it.
In the app, open Tidy tables. A messy sheet gives the wrong answers. Fix it step by step, and watch the answers become right.
Your turn. We explained our finding. What comes next in the loop?
A new question. Remember: data science answers questions with data. Ask, collect, explore, explain, and go round again.

Try it in class tomorrow: ask your pupils for one question about the school that data could answer. Write their ideas on the board. Choose one together that you can measure, and plan what to count this week.
